issues.legal_issue: A court exercising writ jurisdiction may refuse relief when granting it would enable a petitioner to obtain an unjust advantage despite the petitioner’s ability to meet an acknowledged liability.
material_facts: The petitioner personally guaranteed payment of dividends owed by a company and knowingly entered into the guarantee agreement.
The company did not pay the dividends, making the petitioner liable for the amount due.
The petitioner was not shown to lack sufficient funds or personal property to discharge the liability.
The petitioner was given an opportunity to pay before coercive recovery proceedings began but made no attempt to pay.
The petitioner sought writ relief against the recovery proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The petitioner was not entitled to relief, and the appeal was dismissed on that ground without deciding the questions about recovery as arrears of land revenue.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution, the High Court exercises discretionary jurisdiction and may refuse relief where granting it would defeat the interests of justice, secure a dishonest advantage, or perpetuate an unjust gain. The judgment relies on no earlier cases for this principle.

rule.if: writ_relief_case and knowingly_assumed_personal_guarantee and underlying_debt_unpaid and able_to_discharge_liability and made_no_payment_after_opportunity

predicates.writ_relief_case: The person sought relief in a writ proceeding against recovery action for a liability.
predicates.knowingly_assumed_personal_guarantee: The person knowingly undertook personal responsibility for another entity’s payment obligation.
predicates.underlying_debt_unpaid: The entity whose payment was guaranteed did not pay the amount owed.
predicates.able_to_discharge_liability: The person was not shown to lack the funds or property needed to meet the liability.
predicates.made_no_payment_after_opportunity: The person did not attempt to pay after being given an opportunity to do so.

issues.definition: When a person seeks writ relief against recovery of an unpaid guaranteed debt, is able to meet the liability, and makes no payment after an opportunity to do so, the rule provides that writ relief is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A court should give brief reasons when it dismisses a writ petition in limine, particularly when the controversy has not previously been examined by a judicial or quasi-judicial authority.
material_facts: The High Court dismissed the writ petition in limine by a summary order that stated only that it was dismissed.
The controversy had not been processed earlier by an inferior judicial or quasi-judicial authority.
issues.conclusion: The Court stated that it is desirable for a High Court dismissing a writ petition in limine to give a brief statement of reasons, especially when the matter has not previously undergone judicial or quasi-judicial examination.
issues.legal_principle: Because a High Court exercises original jurisdiction under Article 226, a petitioner should know the reasons for an adverse order. Brief reasons promote acceptance of judgments and public confidence in the judicial institution, and assist this Court when special leave is sought. The Court cited no earlier cases for this guidance.

predicates.writ_petition_dismissed_in_limine: A court dismisses a writ petition without proceeding to a full hearing.

issues.definition: When a writ petition is dismissed without a full hearing, the rule states that the dismissal should be accompanied by brief reasons.
